detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) reports that its Division of Cardiovascular Sciences and its Vascular Biology and Hypertension Branch oversee much of the high blood pressure research it funds. Current work described by the institute includes studies of the role of genetics in cardiovascular disease using Framingham Heart Study resources, research into connections between inflammation and high blood pressure, and work on the connection between the microbiome and blood pressure, including a study linking bacterial strains in the mouth to high blood pressure in older women.

NHLBI also describes research on how care is delivered: studies use pharmacy data to identify people who do not refill long-term cardiovascular medicines, as part of work on adherence to medicines that regulate blood pressure. A clinical trial described by the institute, TRIUMPH, found that lifestyle modification such as following the DASH eating plan reduced blood pressure even in people with resistant hypertension. The institute notes continuing work on blood pressure in pregnancy and on reducing disparities in high blood pressure.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about high blood pressure research and clinical trials.

research participation is optional; talk to your doctor about studies
title: Hypertension: where blood pressure research is heading
